Expedited patent examination ₹8,000 instead of ₹60,000; renewal fees also 80% lower
Trademark application or renewal ₹4,500 per class (e-filing) instead of ₹9,000
Lower design registration fees for small entities (amount not confirmed)

Trademarks: upload the Udyam registration certificate when filing
Medium enterprises pay the standard fee

items.name: Collateral-free bank loans for micro and small enterprises (RBI mandate)
items.agency: Reserve Bank of India (applies to all scheduled commercial banks)
items.statusNote: On 6 February 2026 RBI raised the collateral-free limit for MSE loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh, for loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026.
items.headline: Banks may not take collateral on MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh (from 1 Apr 2026)
gets: No collateral security on loans to micro and small enterprises up to ₹20 lakh (previously ₹10 lakh)
A decision on MSME loan applications up to ₹25 lakh within 14 working days
An acknowledgment for every application, and written reasons if it is rejected
checks: Unit must be a micro or small enterprise (Udyam registration)
Applies to loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026; ask the bank to apply the limit
items.docs: Udyam certificate, loan application, KYC, financials

items.name: GST Composition Scheme (Section 10, CGST Act)
items.agency: GST Council / CBIC and State tax departments
items.statusNote: Ongoing statutory option under Section 10 of the CGST Act; opt in at the start of the financial year.
items.headline: Pay GST at a flat 1% (traders, manufacturers) with simple quarterly compliance, turnover up to ₹1.5 crore
gets: Flat tax of 1% of turnover for manufacturers and traders, 5% for restaurants
Service providers with turnover up to ₹50 lakh can pay 6%
Fewer returns and simpler records than regular GST
checks: Aggregate turnover up to ₹1.5 crore in the previous year (₹75 lakh in special category states)
No inter-state outward supplies; not for ice cream, pan masala, tobacco, aerated water or fly ash brick makers
No input tax credit and you cannot collect GST from buyers
Opt in on the GST portal before the start of the financial year
items.docs: GSTIN, turnover records

items.name: Presumptive taxation for small businesses and professionals (s.44AD / s.44ADA, Income-tax Act 1961; s.58, Income-tax Act 2025)
items.agency: Central Board of Direct Taxes, Income Tax Department
items.statusNote: Statutory option. From 1 April 2026 it continues as section 58 of the Income-tax Act 2025 with the same turnover limits and 6%/8% rates (Taxscan, 22 Jun 2026).
items.headline: Declare 6% (digital) or 8% of turnover as profit, no books or audit, turnover up to ₹2 crore (₹3 crore)
gets: Business profit taken as 8% of turnover, or 6% of digital/bank receipts; no detailed books needed
Turnover limit ₹2 crore, or ₹3 crore if cash receipts are within 5%
Professionals (44ADA) can declare 50% of gross receipts as profit, receipts up to ₹50 lakh (higher limit when cash receipts are within 5%)
checks: Only resident individuals, HUFs and partnership firms (not LLPs or companies)
Not for commission, brokerage or agency business; goods carriage operators use a separate rule
If you leave the scheme, you cannot return for the next five years
Choose it when filing the income-tax return
items.docs: Turnover records, bank statements

items.name: Deduction for employment of new employees (s.80JJAA, Income-tax Act 1961; s.146, Income-tax Act 2025)
items.agency: Central Board of Direct Taxes, Income Tax Department
items.statusNote: Statutory deduction; carried into the Income-tax Act 2025 as section 146 from 1 April 2026.
items.headline: Extra tax deduction of 30% of new employees' wages for 3 years (wages up to ₹25,000/month)
gets: Additional deduction of 30% of 'additional employee cost' for three assessment years
In a new business's first year, all eligible wages count
checks: Business must be subject to tax audit (s.44AB) and file the accountant's report before the due date
New employee must earn up to ₹25,000 a month, be in a recognised PF and work at least 240 days (150 days in apparel, footwear, leather)
Total headcount must rise and wages must be paid through bank or electronic modes
Not for businesses formed by split-up, reconstruction or transfer
items.docs: Payroll and PF records, accountant's report

items.name: Authorised Economic Operator programme – special measures for MSMEs (Circular 54/2020-Customs)
items.agency: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
items.statusNote: Ongoing customs programme; MSME relaxations in force since Circular 54/2020-Customs of 15 Dec 2020.
items.headline: Faster customs clearance and lower bank guarantees for MSME importers/exporters with AEO status
gets: Bank guarantee cut to 25% (AEO T1) or 10% (AEO T2) of the normal amount
Priority processing: T1 in 15 working days, T2 in 3 months
checks: MSMEs need only 10 customs documents in the last year (at least 5 each half-year) instead of 25
Two years of business activity and compliance record instead of three
Apply online with MSME annexures
items.docs: IEC, Udyam certificate, customs documents, financial statements, MSME annexures
items.needs: IEC code

items.name: Manufacture and Other Operations in Warehouse Regulations (MOOWR, Sections 58 and 65, Customs Act)
items.agency: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
items.statusNote: Ongoing customs facility, revamped in 2019.
items.headline: Defer customs duty on imported inputs and capital goods; no duty if output is exported
gets: Customs duty on imported raw materials and capital goods deferred until goods are cleared to the domestic market
No duty on imported inputs used in exported goods
No time limit on storage; licence valid until surrendered
No minimum export requirement
checks: Get a private bonded warehouse licence (s.58) with permission to manufacture (s.65)
Apply online with Annexure A and a bond to the jurisdictional Commissioner of Customs
Monthly reports to customs
items.docs: Application (Annexure A), bond, premises documents

items.name: Export Oriented Units Scheme (Foreign Trade Policy 2023, Chapter 6)
items.agency: Department of Commerce / DGFT; Development Commissioners
items.statusNote: Ongoing under Foreign Trade Policy 2023, Chapter 6.
items.headline: Duty-free import and procurement of inputs and capital goods for units that export their output
gets: Duty-free import of capital goods and inputs; IGST and cess exemption on imports
Domestic suppliers get deemed-export benefits; CST reimbursed
Limited sales into the domestic market allowed
100% of export earnings can be kept in an EEFC account
checks: Minimum ₹1 crore in plant and machinery (waived for handicrafts, agriculture, aquaculture, IT, services, handmade jewellery and others)
Must be a positive net foreign exchange earner over 5-year blocks
Trading units not allowed
Apply to the Development Commissioner; sign a Letter of Undertaking
items.docs: Project report, IEC, application to Development Commissioner
items.needs: IEC code

items.name: Software Technology Park (STP) and Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) Schemes
items.agency: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), MeitY
items.statusNote: Ongoing statutory schemes administered by STPI under FTP 2023 Chapter 6.
items.headline: Duty-free import of hardware, software and capital goods for export-oriented IT and electronics units
gets: Fully duty-free import of hardware and software (STP); duty-free inputs and capital goods (EHTP)
Domestic sales allowed up to 50% of export value (STP)
100% foreign equity allowed
checks: Unit must be export-oriented: software and IT services (STP) or electronics hardware (EHTP)
Must achieve positive net foreign exchange earnings
Register online with the nearest STPI centre
items.docs: Company documents, project details, STPI online registration

gets: Product sourcing by TRIFED's 15 regional offices from tribal artisans and SHGs
Sales through TRIBES INDIA outlets, tribesindia.com and exhibitions such as Aadi Mahotsav
Design and onboarding support through partners (NIFT, Meesho)
checks: For tribal (ST) artisans and tribal SHGs
Contact the TRIFED regional office for empanelment and product sampling

50% for SHGs, FPOs, women, SC/ST and differently abled applicants (same cap)
Covers roasters, grinders and mandatory packaging machines
checks: New R&G units, including coffee cafés, with a valid business licence
